summary: This is a Bats test file that sets up a testing environment and then runs two test cases for a function called env::assertFileExists. The setup loads testing libraries and sources the code being tested, then the tests verify that the function properly fails when no file path is configured and succeeds when the file actually exists.

explanations.2: This loads the bats-support library, which provides utility functions that other Bats libraries depend on.
explanations.3: This loads the bats-assert library, which gives us functions like assert_failure and assert_success to verify test outcomes.
explanations.5: This sources (includes) the actual shell script file we're testing, so we can call its functions in our tests.
explanations.9: The 'run' keyword executes the function and captures its output and exit code, so we can check whether it succeeded or failed.
explanations.14: This sets an environment variable that the env::assertFileExists function likely needs to know where to look for the file.
explanations.15: This sets the filename the function will look for, using a unique name (.env.bats.testing) so it doesn't interfere with real .env files.
explanations.16: This creates an empty file at that location so the function will actually find something when it runs.
explanations.17: Now that the file exists and the variables are set, we run the function again to verify it handles the success case correctly.
